cards.explanation: The answer is brothers living together in harmony, friends. David says, "Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!" (Psalm 133:1). Notice he doesn't say it's tolerable or manageable. He says good AND pleasant, both at once. That's a rare combo, like a cookie that's warm and still holds its shape.

The oil reaches over the collar of his robes, friends. David says it runs "…over the collar of his robes." (Psalm 133:2). It doesn't stop at the beard. It keeps on going, and that's the picture David wants us to see. I think that's one generous pour.

The answer is True, friends. David says it's good and pleasant when brothers live together in harmony, and then he says, "It is like fine oil on the head…" (Psalm 133:1-2). The oil is his picture of that harmony. He explains it with something you can almost see and smell.

The answer is True, friends. In the first picture the oil runs down from the head to the beard (Psalm 133:2). In the second, the dew of Hermon is "…falling on the mountains of Zion." (Psalm 133:3). Both of them come down from above. David painted two pictures with one motion.

The blessing is life forevermore, friends. "For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing of life forevermore." (Psalm 133:3). Forevermore is a big word, and David just sets it down quietly at the end. The LORD is the one who bestowed it.

The song calls them to come and bless the LORD, friends. It says, "Come, bless the LORD, all you servants of the LORD who serve by night in the house of the LORD!" (Psalm 134:1). The call goes out to the night servants in particular. They're invited to come and bless Him.

The hands lift up toward the sanctuary, friends. The song says, "Lift up your hands to the sanctuary and bless the LORD!" (Psalm 134:2). The hands go up and the blessing goes to the LORD. Simple as that.

The answer is the LORD, friends. The last line says, "May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion." (Psalm 134:3). The song opened by telling servants to bless the LORD, and it closes with the LORD blessing you. The blessing comes from Him.

The answer is Zion, friends. "May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion." (Psalm 134:3). The Maker of heaven and earth is the One doing the blessing from there. Zion was also where the dew fell in David's picture (Psalm 133:3). Two songs, one place.
